title: Greece's transport ministry presents an AI system that transcribes radio calls between stationmasters and train drivers in real time and checks them against protocols
summary: Greece's deputy transport minister described an AI system from an unnamed supplier that transcribes railway radio calls and checks them against protocols; he gave no measured safety result.
account: Deputy Minister of Transport Konstantinos Kyranakis said that the ministry presented an AI system on Saturday 16 May 2026. SKAI reported his interview about the system on 18 May 2026. In the interview he described a system that transcribes GSM-R communications between stationmasters and train drivers. GSM-R is the digital radio network that railways use. He said that the system would identify departures from railway communication protocols so that the control center could intervene. He called it a new safeguard that works in real time. He contrasted it with investigation after an accident. The interview supplies no developer, operational start date, transcription accuracy, alert counts, or measured safety result.
purpose: The system is intended to monitor operational radio communications and flag departures from protocol for the control center.
system: Speech-to-text and AI protocol-compliance monitoring of GSM-R stationmaster-driver communications (supplier not named)
deployer: Hellenic Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (planned)
taxonomy_note: Announcement only; compliance checking of rail communications is read as a safety detection mechanism.

ai_role.statement: Kyranakis described speech transcription and checks against communication protocols. The original interview does not establish that the system was operating routinely or that an alert prevented an incident.
